name: as-any
description: `as any` erases the type checker at that expression — on money and multi-tenant paths that's where a mispriced charge or a cross-org data leak hides. `(req as any)` and `(req.user as any).id`-style casts have typed replacements (AuthenticatedRequest + req.user.id, getOrganizationId(req)); Express-internals monkey-patches are the residual baseline. This ratchet freezes the count and drives it strictly DOWN — lower baselineCount whenever a reduction lands.
lastBumpNote: 1353 -> 1349 on 2026-08-21: deletion-revealed, not a typing improvement. Four casts went with the PropStream removal (deletion ledger, 2026-08-21) — the two `args as any` in the propstream_lookup / propstream_comps dispatch branches in server/ai/tools.ts, and two `(creds as any).mlsUrl` reads in services/connectors/executor.ts that the new `resoBaseUrl(creds)` helper replaced with a typed narrowing. The remaining connector dispatch branches keep their `args as any` and stay in this baseline; they are still reachable. Locked in per the strictly-down rule. PRIOR NOTE — 1354 -> 1353 on 2026-08-20: the dispatch branch for `batch_leads_skip_trace` in server/ai/tools.ts carried `args as any`, and the branch was deleted with the executor behind it (deletion ledger, 2026-08-20). Deletion-revealed, not a typing improvement: the FCRA gate added the day before returns before that switch, so the branch had been unreachable since it landed, and Pax was the executor's only caller. The four sibling connector branches keep their `args as any` and stay in this baseline — they are still reachable. Locked in per the strictly-down rule. PRIOR NOTE — 1355 -> 1354 on 2026-08-19: deletion-revealed, not a refactor. `atlasContextInjector.ts`, `communicationDeduplication.ts` and `userAiCostControls.ts` were deleted (deletion ledger 2026-08-19) after lint-reachability was taught to strip comments and showed all three were module orphans — each had been reading as imported because its own docblock opened with a usage example the scanner took for real code. Two of the three carried the same lazy-Redis shape (`let _redis: any`, `Promise<any | null>`, `const IORedis = (await import("ioredis")).default`), which is where these counts came from. Locked in per the strictly-down rule: the reduction belongs to the commit that earned it.  PRIOR NOTE — 1356 -> 1355 on 2026-08-19: routes-data-intelligence reads organizations.underwritingDefaults through its declared $type instead of casting to any, so a renamed section is a type error rather than a silent undefined. The landDeal section added in the same commit needed no cast for the same reason.
minimaNote: VACUITY FLOOR on the SCAN POPULATION, not a ratchet. baselineCount above counts BAD THINGS FOUND, so a scan that stops seeing files finds zero and reports it as progress: a zero baseline PASSes on an empty file set, and a nonzero one prints a stale-high "lock it in" for a number that was never true. MEASURED 2026-08-16: this config matched 1370 file(s) (server/**/*.ts minus tests). Floor set to 1100, comfortably below that, so a broken glob or walk trips it while ordinary deletion does not. Checked BEFORE the baseline comparison by scripts/ratchet.mjs; a MISSING floor fails as loudly as a breached one. If a real deletion wave shrinks this population, lower the floor in the same commit and name the wave here — never raise it to silence something, never delete the key. Re-measure with `node scripts/ratchet.mjs --measure`.
